units.text: INT. BEEKEEPER'S SHED - NIGHT
A low, windowless hut of unplaned planks.
Rows of honey jars glow amber in the lantern light.
From the hives outside, a drone, deep and constant.
The walls tremble with it.
ONDINE HAWTHORNE, 30s, in a veil and cotton gloves, sets a jar on the shelf and wipes her hands, never turning from the door.
Her brother MORDECAI, 40s, bearded, bare-armed, stands in the doorway with a smoker in one hand and a bucket in the other.
Neither has spoken for some time.
He steps inside; she steps back.
The bucket slips from his fingers and spills a thick gold river across the floor, and as she reaches for a rag he catches her wrist.
The lantern gutters.
Behind them the humming rises, and the tallest hive outside begins, very quietly, to speak her name.
Let go.
units.name: ONDINE

units.text: They want you back.
units.name: MORDECAI

units.text: They want what's in me.
units.name: ONDINE

units.text: He releases her.
She backs against the shelf.
The jars chime against each other.
The humming stops.
In the new silence, a single bee crawls from the neck of her veil and walks across her cheek.
